# https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/overview

Source: https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/overview

SurrealDB supports multiple authentication methods designed for different use cases, from server administration to end-user access in client-side applications.
  * •
[System users](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/authentication#system-users) — administrator-managed accounts with role-based access control at the root, namespace, or database level.
  * •
[Record users](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/authentication#record-users) — application users that sign up and sign in through custom logic, restricted by table and field permissions.
  * •
[Sessions](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/authentication#sessions) — persistent connections that carry authentication state, with configurable token and session expiration.
  * •
[JSON Web Tokens](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/summary#json-web-tokens) — internal token management and third-party provider integration via JWKS.

For a condensed reference of all authentication-related features and links, see the [Summary](https://surrealdb.com/docs/learn/security/authentication/summary) page.
